title: Only one flaw
body:
It’s a great habit tracker app. There’s just one thing I find frustrating.  If you allow multiple check ins when you’re creating a card, you have to set a number. If you don’t hit that number, you “missed your goal”. 
If you don’t allow multiple check ins, you can’t add a “bonus” check in.  
I have lots of daily goals that I’d like to have as “at least once /day” but allow for more check ins if I am able to do them again that day. 
It would be SO much better if the option to add multiple check ins was open ended. 
Set the goal at whatever you want it to be but also allow for extra “bonus” check ins.
*edited to add* I bought the premium edition almost right away.

title: Solid habit tracker with nice features and some room for improvement
body:
I have looked through most habit trackers on the app store, and so far this seems like the one I will likely settle on long-term.  The interface is attractive and the “cards” for building your own HUD for each habit is a nice touch.  I also appreciate the daily overview of all habits and the Apple Watch companion app.  

I cannot quite give it 5 stars though for a few misc. reasons.  One, although it has a quite good Watch app from my testing so far, the lack of more comprehensive complication options is a hindrance.  (Devs, please add complications that work with Infograph Modular in particular!  This is huge for me!)

As well, the GUI, while pretty and generally responsive, suffers a bit from having unusually fiddly buttons.  Either they are too small or the touch sensitivity for them is too low, because I find myself having to press them repeatedly at times to get a response.  I also feel that the New Cards and New Task guis could be streamlined a bit, or at least made more tap-friendly.  They feel a bit awkward to move through quickly, mostly for the same reason of fiddly unresponsive buttons.

As well, I find the swiping behaviour on the main task face a bit unresponsive as well.  It is heavily biased towards up-down swipes and I have to try multiple times to get left/right swiping between tasks to work properly.  Better swipe direction detection would help a lot.

I think my only other minor complaint is that it would be nice if Task screens were a bit more customizable.  The photos are nice, but having the task title all the way at screen bottom and with no text-background option means some photos are hard to read against, or that usable screen real estate goes largely unused (having the option to pin a card there would be nice for instance).  I also somewhat miss the ability to use glyphs for tasks that I have seen in some other habit trackers.

Beyond these quibbles/rough edges, I appreciate the app’s commitment to privacy, on-device data, its’ reasonable pricing, and its’ interesting mix of variable simplicity and customizability.  I have not so far run into any noticeable bugs beyond the minor UI frustrations.  I would love to see more extensive Card options per task, and more Health metric integration, and some Widgets.  Possibly more chart and graph options would also be nice, but I think the current ones do a respectable job, that said.

In summary, I think this is a solid app for the price that provides an enjoyable experience grounded in an appealing design.

title: I adore this straightforward habit/goal app
body:
Thanks! I am finding Today to be a very simple and intuitive habit forming app. It’s flexible to handle every goal you can imagine, and forces me to keep it concise.

I like that I can choose a personal photo as the background image for each goal — I was surprised that this added significant extra inspiration for each item compared to other goal/habit apps I’ve tried.

Another favourite feature is the ability to add the “journal/notes” and “photo gallery” cards, used to inspire me later on when I need to remember how to meet that goal! 

One last thing: I am so stoked I can access this tool, support your work at a fair and upfront cost, without signing up for a subscription! Thanks again, I do strongly recommend this app.

title: Beautiful Goal-tracker
body:
I love this app! It’s exactly what I was looking for, and the one time premium is totally worth the $$. I don’t understand why so many of these apps are subscription based, so it’s nice to find an app that covers all the features without the ongoing price tag. The interface is smooth and attractive. It’s very simple to use. And yet there are also some nice in depth features if you want to go detailed. There is a convenient streak calendar, separate for each goal. You can keep a journal, track steps and other iOS Health stats, and even create your own custom milestones (such as reaching a certain weight, finishing a study list, or reading a certain number of books). I highly recommend.

My only suggestion is that I would like to be able to colour code or create categories in the overview section.

But when I check into my watch it will still have the previous days check-in on there, and when it finally syncs up and I am able to check in from the watch, that information is not transferred to my phone. I think it’s working, and when I check my phone, sometimes the same day, sometimes 2 days later it’s unchecked and I have to fill it in from my phone. I would like to not have to open my phone to make sure I have the check-in. It defeats the purpose of why I got it. Please fix this problem, and it will be 5 stars in my books!

title: What I needed
body:
I love this app. It pushes me to be consistent. I have 8 or 9 habits that I'm juggling, and although some I can't complete, the ones I do complete like daily push-ups, cold showers, and runs every few days make me feel like a changed person. I have a few minor problems with the app, for example, the fluidity of the switching between habits could be smoother as I can only seem to swipe left or right once I've scrolled all the way to the very top of the habit page, but for the most part, the app runs great. I hope to see an update where more cards, covers, and features in general are introduced, but for the most part, the app is already really great. All in all, I give Today an A, but it still has room to improve on before I can give it an A+. I think that an A+ is possible with the current direction, ideas, and feel, so what it needs to work on is simply more features and polish. Keep it up. 

Thanks.
